rows.title: Dialects — Why
rows.summary: Why
body: - A new target is data files, templates and tests, not a new compiler.
- A dialect decides only how the output is written; the `.nuc` never changes with it.
- It never reads target code and never wraps the target's libraries.

rows.title: The `dart` dialect — Rules of this project
rows.summary: `[decorators.args]`, `[architecture.names]`, call sites); a need of this target is asked as a generic `[options]` key or template variable (the language project decides it).
body: - **The `.nuc` never bends to Dart.** Names are written as they are: Nuclear's `camelCase` is Dart's.
- **Nothing of Dart or Flutter in Rust.** Generic mechanisms belong in the compiler (projects, `decor`,
`[decorators.args]`, `[architecture.names]`, call sites); a need of this target is asked as a generic `[options]`
key or template variable (the language project decides it). Flutter specifics live here, as data.
- **The library is Nuclear's.** Every member of [the standard library](../../docs/07-reference/library.md) has its
template in `library.toml`; a Dart name in Nuclear code, in a reference or in an example is a bug.
- **A framework dialect only writes the platform.** A kind, a decorator or a folder is added to the platform's
contract first; `frameworks/flutter/` adds how it is written in Dart (ADR-dart-0001).
- The generated code is what an expert would write: `const` constructors, no layer that adds nothing at run time;
- The automatic imports of the SDK and of the packages come from the type definitions (`[dialect] defs`), not from
hand-written lists. An `[auto_imports]` entry exists only for a package without definitions (`fpdart`, the test
libraries) or to choose the module of a name two packages export.

rows.summary: Kinds
body: | `statemodel` | `statemodel.tpl` | the states of a screen: `<Name>Status`, the constructors `Name.field(...)`, `Name.initial()`, and a typed `<Name>Builder` over `BlocBuilder` |

| `statemanager` | `statemanager.tpl`, `statemanager_method.tpl`, `statemanager_signature.tpl` | a Cubit (`StateManager`) built with `super(const S.initial())`; a `@state(S.field)` method emits that state, and with a `Result` it emits the error with the `Err` |
| `form` | `form.tpl` | a form model: fields, rules (`Rule`, `Rules`), initial values |
| `formmanager` | `formmanager.tpl` | a `FormManager<F>` built with `super(F.rules, F.initial, F.fromValues)`; `@validate("field")` methods are remote validations |

| `tests` | `tests.tpl`, `tests_method.tpl` | a `flutter_test` group: `@test` → `test(...)`, `@widget` → `testWidgets(...)`, `@states` → `blocTest(...)` (`seed`, `wait`, `skip`, `expect`); a method without a decorator is `setUp`, `tearDown`, `setUpAll` or `tearDownAll`; `@mock([X])` creates a mocktail mock of `X` and puts it in the injector; `X.m()` is `inject<X>().m()`; a `Result` is kept, not propagated |

rows.title: What each kind of `flutter` generates — Kinds
rows.summary: Kinds
body: | `stateless` | `stateless.tpl` | a `StatelessWidget` with a `const` constructor (`{super.key, ...}`, named parameters as `final` fields); `build` and the other members get `@override` |

| `stateful` | `stateful.tpl` | a `StatefulWidget` and its `State`: fields, methods and mixins (`with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin`) go to the `State`; the parameters stay in the widget and are read as `widget.name` (`param_access`) |

| `@screen(providers = [...])` on a view | the same templates | the widget wraps a private `_<Name>View` in a `MultiBlocProvider` with one `BlocProvider<Manager>(create: (_) => inject<Manager>())` per provider; `Manager.load()` in the view is `context.read<Manager>().load()` |

| `model` | `model.tpl` | an immutable class with a `const` constructor, `fromJson` / `toJson` written by json_serializable (`@JsonSerializable(explicitToJson: true)`, `part '<file>.g.dart';`) and equality. A generic model (`Page<T>`) uses `genericArgumentFactories`. `@key("json_name")` is the field's name in the JSON; `@Converter` on a field is the converter that reads and writes it |

rows.title: What each kind of `flutter` generates — Kinds
rows.summary: Kinds
body: | `model` with `@primary` | `model.tpl` (`field_decor`) | `static final LocalTable<M> table`, named by `@entity("table")` (`decor.entity.arg`; the model's name in `snake_case` without it); `@created` / `@updated` are stamped by the table. It is registered with its component in `registerSynapsis` (`Local.register(M.table, component: ...)`) |
| `converter` | `converter.tpl` | a `JsonConverter<T, J>`; `T` and `J` come from the `fromJson` signature; `sample()` is optional, for the generated tests |

| `repository` | `repository.tpl`, `repository_method.tpl` | a `Repository` subclass; each method without a body and with `@get` / `@post` / `@put` / `@patch` / `@delete` is a `send(...)` call (path, query or body from the parameters, `Decode`, `Cache`, `retry`). A cached method also generates `purge<Method>()`. A method with a body is a plain Dart method |

| `usecase` | `injectable.tpl`, `usecase_method.tpl` | a class with its injected dependencies and one `exec`; `@requires(...)` → `Guards.check(...)` and `@acl(...)` → `await Guards.verify(...)` (`Guards.check(...)` when `exec` is not async) at the start of `exec`, returning `Left(...)` when denied |
| `appcomponent` | `injectable.tpl` | aliases to the use cases through `inject` (`alias_via = "inject"`) |
| `service`, `aggregate`, `component` | `injectable.tpl` | a plain class with its injected dependencies |

rows.title: The `flutter` dialect: the mobile platform written in Dart — What it changes of `dart`
rows.summary: (dependencies.md).
body: - `defs`: the Flutter SDK, the runtime and the libraries it relies on, added to `dart`'s
([dependencies.md](dependencies.md)). Their names are imported automatically, their classes can be extended
(`Counter: Cubit<int>`) and their inherited members are used without declaring them (`emit`, `state`).
- `replaces`: in Synapsis, `WebSocket` is the connection of the project config, not the `dart:io` class; the
Genkit names the package `synapsis_genkit` re-exports (`Tool`, `Message`, `Genkit`, `Part`...) are imported

- **A framework dialect only writes the platform.** A kind, a decorator or a folder is added to the platform's
